relatedSnapshot.title: Rep scoreboard counts unique people by phone number, so shared numbers undercount reached contacts
relatedSnapshot.description:
> **Verified 2026-08-18 against origin/main c2ed730b4e.** The code defect is confirmed verbatim, but the ticket's premise was wrong: `getCallScoreboard` has no client consumer, so no rep or manager reads this number today — rewritten as a latent defect to fix before the surface ships.
> AC5 is descoped (there is no surface on which to state the metric's meaning) and priority drops to Medium. The `crm_event` index anchor pointed at the wrong index and is corrected below.

> **Re-verified 2026-08-19 against origin/main e3f64a2b2a** (intake gate). The defect and the "latent, not live" framing both hold: `getCallScoreboard` still has no client consumer, no ENG-12447 child renders it, and no Floor Command PR reimplements the metric — so Backlog/Medium stands. Corrected in this pass: all three line anchors (they drifted +1 when #6052 merged), every production figure, the `crm_event` evidence (92% of it turns out not to be phone calls), and the scope/test plan (the DB test already exists, and is a shadow-SQL harness). The AC2 fork is now resolved rather than left open. A second defect in the same expression (it counts people *dialled*, not *reached*) was raised, researched and **settled from the record without needing the Product Owner** — see "Resolved" at the end.

Found during the portfolio-wide ticket audit on 2026-08-13, re-verified 2026-08-18. No existing ticket covers this.

## The defect

`apps/web/lib/crm/my-day-call-scoreboard-service.ts:185-186` computes `uniquePeopleReached` as `COUNT(DISTINCT callTable.toNumber)` straight off `callTable`, ignoring the `crm_event` contact link entirely. The metric is named "unique **people**" but keyed on a **phone number**. Verbatim on `main`, unchanged since filing.

## Corrected 2026-08-18 — this is latent, not live

The original text called this "a rep-facing performance figure". It is not one yet, and that changes the urgency, not the fix.

`MyDayCallScoreboardService` has exactly one caller: the `getCallScoreboard` tRPC procedure (`apps/web/trpc/routers/crm/my-day.ts:489`, instantiated at `:497`). **Nothing in the app calls** `getCallScoreboard` — no component, hook, page or route references it; the only references outside the router are its tests. The scoreboard the UI actually renders is `getCloserScoreboard` (`:424`), backed by a different service (`apps/web/lib/crm/my-day-closer-scoreboard-service.ts`) which does not compute this metric at all. `uniquePeopleReached` appears nowhere outside the service file (`:28`, `:42`, `:86`, `:185`).

So nobody reads a wrong number today. ENG-11568 shipped the query and endpoint only (#5960, Done 2026-08-11) and said so in its own PR boundary — *"The screen, pipeline split and non-call activity are separate work."* This is a defect to fix **before** that screen lands, and it is cheapest to fix now, while the only consumer is a test.

## Why the number would be wrong once surfaced

A phone number is not a person in this data. Re-measured against the production replica on 2026-08-19 (the 2026-08-18 pass could not re-run these).

**All figures below are digit-normalised** — `regexp_replace(number,'[^0-9]','','g')` over non-deleted `crm_telephone` rows that have a contact — and they are deliberately approximate: `crm_telephone` takes roughly 150 new rows a day, so every one of them drifts upward daily. Snapshot 2026-08-19 11:41Z.

* **\~2,300 numbers are shared by two or more contacts** (2,295 at the snapshot; 2,294 thirty-five minutes earlier). The 2026-08-13 figure of 2,118, and its 1,886/193/27/6/5/1 breakdown, reproduces under no method tried and should not be cited.
* **Up to 30 contacts sit on a single number** — not 7.
* **41 contacts hold two or more distinct numbers.** Each inflates the count when a rep reaches the same person on two lines.
* Separately, **10,329 contacts hold a phone row that normalises to zero digits** — a data-quality problem rather than a shared number, and out of scope here.

On the raw-string basis the first and third figures are 2,063 and 66, and the raw "maximum" of 10,293 is simply the empty-string bucket — an artefact, not a real shared number. That is why the normalised basis is the one quoted. **Do not mix the two bases:** an earlier revision of this ticket quoted 2,063 alongside a normalised max of 30 and 41, which made the figures look mutually inconsistent.

The load-bearing claim is the shape, not the digits: numbers are shared, contacts hold several, so keying the metric on a number miscounts in both directions.

So the number would be wrong in both directions — but *would be*, not *is*. These are contact-book statistics, not call-log statistics; see the denominator caveat below.

## The link it should use already exists

Call → contact resolution is already stored at write time on `crm_event`, not re-derived: `crm_event.entity_id` with `entity_type = 'contact'` and `type = 'call'`. On 2026-08-19 production held ~1,242 such rows across ~918 distinct contacts (1,243 an hour later — this drifts too) — **but 1,140 of those 1,242 carry** `source = 'recall_calendar'`. They are meeting-recording events, and **zero of them join to any** `call` **row**. Only ~54 rows are genuine call→contact links. The raw 1,242 must not be read as evidence that the link is well populated: 92% of it is not phone calls at all. Any implementation must therefore join on `callSid`, never on `type`/`entity_type` alone.

**Link coverage, measured 2026-08-19 (never measured before).** 54 of 105 `call` rows (51%) resolve to a `crm_event` contact link; for the `direction = 'outbound'` rows this scoreboard actually aggregates, 6 of 7. All 54 matched events are `entity_type = 'contact'`. The matcher deliberately refuses to guess — `lookupContactByPhone` uses `.limit(2)` and returns `'ambiguous'` rather than picking (`apps/web/lib/crm/contact-phone-lookup.ts:81`, `:88`) — so the link is trustworthy where it exists. **But read the other half of that sentence too** (added 2026-08-19, from independent review): where the number is ambiguous, no link is written *at all*. That is the flip side of the same refusal, and it is what bounds this fix — see "What this actually fixes" below.

**Denominator caveat.** Production's entire `call` table is **105 rows — 7 of them outbound** — across 3 organisations and 2 distinct `to_number`s, spanning 2026-08-07 to 2026-08-17. The dialler went live twelve days ago, and **no rep has yet dialled a shared number**. That is an argument for fixing this now, while it is cheap and the only consumer is a test — not evidence that anyone is reading a wrong figure today.

**Join key, added 2026-08-18.** `call` has no `contact_id` (`packages/db/src/schema/voice.ts:63-113`) — adding one is ENG-12257's job. The join available today is `call.provider_call_sid` (`voice.ts:76`) to `crm_event.metadata->'data'->>'callSid'` (`packages/db/src/schema-support/crm-event.ts:112`).

**Index anchor, corrected 2026-08-18.** The old text cited `packages/db/src/schema/crm.ts:1630-1634` for a partial index added by #5878. That anchor has drifted — 1630-1634 is now `crm_message_delivery_status_history_*` — and, more importantly, the index it named (`crm_event_outbound_call_history_idx`, now at `crm.ts:1862-1866`) is keyed `(organization_id, entity_id, created_at desc)` for listing **one contact's** call history. It does nothing for this aggregation.

The index that does serve the join already exists: `crm_event_org_call_sid_active_unique` (`crm.ts:1878-1882`), unique on `(organization_id, (metadata->'data'->>'callSid'))` where `type = 'call'` and the row is not deleted. **So this fix needs no migration and no new index.**

## Why this is not ENG-12257

ENG-12257 has an acceptance criterion covering exactly this metric — its AC3, *"Counting how many different people a rep dialled in a day is a single query with no phone-number matching"* — but it was written on 2026-08-03 and **#5960 shipped the wrong implementation on 2026-08-11, eight days later**, so re-pointing the query is out of that ticket's stated scope. ENG-12257 is also still blocked — but by ENG-12663 alone, since ENG-12255 was completed on 2026-08-14, and covers a much larger change: stored `contact_id`/`deal_id` columns on `call`, populated at every call site, plus a throttled backfill. This fix needs none of that — it can use the `crm_event` link that is already there.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `uniquePeopleReached` counts distinct contacts, resolved through the `crm_event` call→contact link, not `COUNT(DISTINCT to_number)`. *(The field was also renamed to* `uniquePeopleDialed` *in the same PR — see "Resolved" below. AC1–AC4 are written against the original name because that is what they were adjudicated against.)*
2. A call whose contact could not be resolved unambiguously is counted once and is not silently merged with a different person who shares the number.
3. A contact reached on two different numbers within the window counts once.
4. A regression test covers the shared-number case: two contacts on one number produce two reached people, not one.

### What this actually fixes — scope of AC2 and AC4 (added 2026-08-19, independent review)

**AC2 and AC4 hold for calls placed with an explicit** `contactId`**, and not for the ambiguous-number webhook path.** This does not make the fix wrong — it is strictly better than keying on the number for every row — but the original text read as though shared numbers were solved outright, and they are not.

Calls linked *after the fact* by the Twilio status webhook get their contact from `apps/web/app/api/voice/status/route.ts:339-343` → `findContactIdByPhone` → `findContactByPhone` (`apps/web/lib/crm/contact-phone-lookup.ts:91-102`), which returns `null` unless `lookupContactByPhone` says `'unique'`. So on an **ambiguous** number — two contacts sharing it, which is exactly the population this ticket exists for — no `crm_event` link is written, both calls fall into the same `num:` bucket, and the two people merge.

Concretely: contacts A and B share `<phone>`; a rep keypad-dials it four times; `uniquePeopleDialed` reports **1**, identical to the pre-fix behaviour. The click-to-call path is unaffected, because the dialer supplies `contactId` directly (`apps/web/trpc/routers/crm/communication.ts:1266-1272`).

**This inverts the impact story the ticket originally told.** AC3 — one contact reached on two numbers — is fully fixed, and applies to **41** contacts. AC4 — two contacts on one number — is the common case at ~2,300 numbers, and is only fixed where an explicit link exists. The rare case is the one that is completely solved.

**Follow-up to file:** resolve the ambiguous-number case. It cannot be done by phone matching (that is the matching this metric exists to avoid, and it is unsafe on precisely these numbers). The durable answer is ENG-12257's stored `call.contact_id`, populated at the call site where the identity is known rather than re-derived later.

**A second, smaller trade-off, now pinned by a test:** one person occupies two buckets when only some of their calls in the window carry a link — a keypad dial writes `entity_type='organization'` (`CONTACTLESS_CALL_ENTITY_TYPE`, `communication.ts:156`), which the join excludes. Click-to-call contact A, then keypad-dial the same number: the old expression gave 1, this one gives 2. Accepted deliberately, and asserted so it cannot flip silently.

*Former AC5 — "the metric's meaning is stated where it is surfaced, so 'reached' is not read as 'dialled'" — is descoped as unsatisfiable: there is no surface to label. It belongs with whichever* ENG-12447 *child renders this table, alongside the screen itself.*

## Decision for the implementer — the unresolved-call bucket key

AC2 admits more than one reading, and the choice is a real semantics fork worth settling before coding.

`COALESCE(crm_event.entity_id, 'call:' || call.id)` gives every unresolved call its own bucket. That satisfies AC2 literally — two people sharing a number are never merged — but it **inflates** the count when one unknown person is dialled repeatedly: ten attempts on the same unrecognised number read as ten people reached.

The alternative is to fall back to the number for unresolved calls (`COALESCE(entity_id, 'num:' || call.to_number)`), which keeps repeat dials in one bucket but reintroduces the shared-number merge for exactly those unresolved rows. No option avoids both. **Resolved 2026-08-19: use the number fallback** — `COALESCE(entity_id, 'num:' || call.to_number)`.

The deciding evidence is the reference implementation ENG-12257 names: Close's call reports define the equivalent metric as "unique leads **dialed** versus repeat dials, helpful when comping on unique dials". Collapsing repeat dials is the entire purpose of the metric, and the `'call:' || call.id` bucket does the exact opposite. Number-fallback confines the shared-number merge to the rows we have no link for — a strictly smaller wrong than today's, which applies to every row. The measured 51% link coverage does not decide this on its own (n=105 is far too small), so the decision rests on the reference rather than on the data. **Correction, 2026-08-19:** an earlier revision of this line claimed no `COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(...))` precedent exists in the repo. That was wrong — it came from a too-literal grep for that exact string. The idiom has **two** precedents:

* `apps/web/lib/crm/communication-fields.ts:119-126` — `COUNT(DISTINCT type || ':' || COALESCE(..., id::text))`: a prefixed string sentinel mixed with real ids in a single DISTINCT, in the same directory.
* `apps/web/lib/services/recall-calendar-recording-overview-stats.ts:88-91` — `count(distinct ...)` over `coalesce(contact.id::text, lower(trim(attendee.email)))`: the identical "entity id, else raw identifier" shape for a people count, without even a prefix.

So this is an established house idiom rather than a novel construction, and ours is strictly safer than the recall precedent — a UUID rendered as text cannot collide with a `num:`-prefixed string. Still state the choice in a comment on the query and pin it with the AC4 test.

## Scope and shape

Estimated ~110 lines across 4 files, no migration and no new index:

* `apps/web/lib/crm/my-day-call-scoreboard-service.ts` — the aggregate query and its row type
* `apps/web/tests/lib/crm/my-day-call-scoreboard-service.test.ts` — unit coverage
* `apps/web/tests/lib/crm/my-day-call-scoreboard-db.test.ts` — **this file already exists.** The earlier claim that a DB test must be created, with `my-day-incoming-leads-db.test.ts` as its precedent, was wrong.

⚠️ **The existing DB test cannot serve as AC4 evidence as written.** At ~:100 it hand-copies the aggregate SQL — including `COUNT(DISTINCT to_number)` — and compares that copy against the service. A shadow-SQL harness like that compares two copies of the same expression, so it would pass while the metric stayed wrong. AC4 needs **literal expected-count assertions**: seed two contacts sharing one number, assert the service returns 2.

No open PR touches `my-day-call-scoreboard*` or `apps/web/trpc/routers/crm/my-day.ts` — 150 open PRs swept by file tree on 2026-08-19. #6052, the one collision this ticket previously named, **merged on 2026-08-19** and is what shifted the line anchors above, so that note is now historical. This change should not need the router at all, since the procedure's shape is unchanged.

## Notes

Priority lowered to Medium on 2026-08-18. The P2/High justification was that this is "a rep-facing performance figure", and that does not hold — the endpoint has no consumer and the metric reaches no screen. It should rise again the moment an ENG-12447 child wires this table to a surface.

Recommended owner: whoever holds ENG-12447 (Anuj) may still be the better home, since ENG-11568 was re-parented there and this is its metric. Filed here so it is not lost; reassign freely.

## Resolved 2026-08-19 — "reached" vs "dialled" (settled from the record; James not consulted)

The aggregate carries no `FILTER (WHERE connected)`, so `uniquePeopleReached` counts people **dialled**, not **reached**. This was logged as a question for the Product Owner. It is answered by the existing record and does not need him.

**Answer: the computation is right and the NAME is wrong. Keep it unfiltered; rename it into the "dialled" family.**

Evidence:

* **The vocabulary is already defined.** ENG-12250 (James Keeble, 2026-08-03): *"Dial = one outbound call attempt. Connect = a dial where a human picked up."*
* **The AC that governs this metric says "dialled".** ENG-12257 AC3 (James Keeble, 2026-08-03): *"Counting how many different people a rep **dialled** in a day is a single query with no phone-number matching"* — and it names Close's *"Unique leads dialed"* as the reference implementation. Close's own doc: *"unique leads dialed versus repeat dials."*
* **The code was built as a sibling of** `dials`**, deliberately.** `connects` (`:174`), `talkTimeSec` (`:178`) and `meaningfulConversations` (`:182`) each carry `FILTER (WHERE connectedCall)`. Only `dials` (`:172`) and `uniquePeopleReached` (`:186`) omit it — applied three times, omitted twice.
* **Nothing renders it.** "Design · Screen 4 — SDR pipeline", attached to both ENG-12447 and ENG-12490, has columns `SDR | Dials | Connects | Pickup rate | Talk time | Texts | Meetings set | Setter show | Pay support booked | Collected`. There is no unique-people column under any name, and ENG-12490's own metric list matches. No user-visible label is at stake.

**The decisive point against the current name:** "reached" is *already* a defined, user-visible term in this codebase, and it means **connected**. `reachedOnlyPredicate()` (`apps/web/lib/crm/call-history-fields.ts:106-113`) defines Reached as a `crm_event` outcome of answered / completed / connected, and it backs `lastReachedAt`, surfaced in both the contact and deal filter registries (`filter-field-registry.ts:381-386`, `:587-590`) as **"Last reached" — "most recent outbound call whose final outcome is answered, completed, or connected"**. So `uniquePeopleReached` is not merely loose wording: it collides with an existing product definition of the same word. Renaming resolves the AC3 mismatch and the collision together.

Counter-evidence, recorded rather than suppressed: ENG-11568 (James Keeble, 2026-07-13) does say *"unique people reached"* — once, in prose, with no acceptance criterion covering the metric, and the same author wrote "dialled" for it three weeks later.

Note for anyone tempted by the other branch: a connected-filtered unique-people count would **not** be redundant. `connects` is `COUNT(*)` over rows — calls, not people — so no existing column carries unique-people-connected. If that metric is ever wanted it is a **new column**, not a redefinition of this one.

**Done in #6069**, folded in rather than filed as a follow-up. A separate PR would have needed its own Name 1 ticket purely to satisfy the one-token gate, and the field is dead-ended — no consumer, no label, no design — so the rename carried no user-facing risk. It was made before any human review began, so no approval was invalidated.

**Final identifier:** `uniquePeopleDialed`**, single-l.** The repo conflicts with this ticket's Name 2 spelling and the repo won: identifiers are uniformly single-l (`dialedDigits`, `setDialedDigits`, `MAX_DIALED_DIGITS`, aria-label "Dialed keypad digits") with zero double-l identifiers, while all four `dialled` occurrences in the repo are prose inside comments. So the code follows that split — identifier `uniquePeopleDialed`, prose keeps "dialled".

Still deliberately out of scope: the connected filter. Only the name changed; the computation is untouched.

## Query plan: why the contact join stays a plain LEFT JOIN (measured 2026-08-19)

Recorded here rather than in a source comment — planner costs rot on the first plan change and a reviewer cannot verify them in a diff.

A cleanup pass flagged that this join can plan as a **hash left join** whose `crm_event` build side carries no time bound, while the `call` side is windowed — so the build set is every active call event the organisation has ever produced, carrying the full `metadata` jsonb (`width=495`, avg 479 B) into the hash table. Real, but the prescribed fix was measured on the replica and declined:

* At production's actual call volume the plain join **already plans as a nested loop**, with the full two-column `Index Cond` on `crm_event_org_call_sid_active_unique`. The hash plan appears only as the *outer* side grows — flip point around **100 rows**, reproduced synthetically at 100 / 500 / 1k / 2k / 5k / 20k / 50k.
* **A bare** `LEFT JOIN LATERAL` **buys nothing.** At 50k it produced a byte-identical hash plan, because Postgres pulls the subquery back up. The `width=16` improvement comes from `LIMIT 1` acting as an optimisation fence, not from LATERAL.
* Forcing the nested loop is currently **\~2x more expensive**: hash `30.11` against forced `63.74` at 1k calls, against the real `crm_event` side.
* `LIMIT 1` is therefore the only form that changes the plan — and it would silence fan-out detection (a broken predicate would silently pick one of N rows instead of inflating `dials`) and make the `type='call'` negative control nondeterministic.

**Revisit condition:** one organisation's active call events approaching `work_mem` — roughly 55k rows at ~495 B. The largest organisation holds **233** today. The durable fix is ENG-12257's `call.contact_id`, which deletes this join outright.

One further note for whoever revisits: the planner estimates `rows=1` for the build side where the real count is 50, because `crm_event` carries no extended statistics and multiplies `type='call'` × `entity_type='contact'` × `organization_id` as independent when they are heavily correlated. That is a correlation artefact rather than a small-table one, so it will persist as the table grows.

**Verified against production, 2026-08-19:** `crm_event_org_call_sid_active_unique` exists with `indisunique = t` and `indisvalid = t`, its definition matches the schema byte-for-byte, and the maximum number of active `type='call'` events per `(organization_id, callSid)` is **1**. It is 19 if soft-deleted and NULL-sid rows are included — both of which the join excludes — so the partial predicates are load-bearing rather than decorative. Worth confirming explicitly given this repo's history of guarded index migrations silently skipping; this one (`packages/db/migrations/20260806125602_abandoned_jack_power.sql:92-95`) raises rather than skips, and the index is present.

Also measured: all 1,255 production `crm_event` rows of `type='call'` are `entity_type='contact'` — there are **zero** `organization` rows today. The `entity_type` predicate is still correct to have (contactless dials write that shape), but it currently guards a population that exists in code rather than in data.

relatedSnapshot.title: Show who is calling when a phone number belongs to more than one contact
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When a prospect calls back and their number is saved on more than one contact, the incoming call card shows "Unknown caller" and "No matching contact", and the call never appears on anyone's timeline. Reps should see who is calling, and the call should land on the right record.

## Problem

A rep in the AIA Sales Team workspace left a voicemail, the prospect called back 7 minutes later, and the rep had no idea who it was (Slack report with screenshot).

The prospect exists twice in the CRM with the same phone number: once from a webinar signup and once from a purchase made with a different email. When a number matches more than one contact, the app refuses to choose and treats the caller as unknown. The card then says "No matching contact", which is untrue: there were two matches.

This is common. In that workspace 1,004 phone numbers are shared by more than one contact (2,077 contacts).

## User experience

Today:

* A known prospect calls back. The card title reads "Unknown caller", shows only the number, and says "No matching contact".
* After the call, the call and its recording are not on the prospect's timeline, because they were saved with no contact.

Expected:

* The card names the people who share the number, for example "Name 4 or Name 3", with the one the team was most recently in touch with shown first, and a line reading "2 matching contacts".
* The call and its recording appear on the timeline of the contact the team was most recently in touch with on that number.

## What's included

* Incoming call card: show the matching contacts' names when a number matches more than one contact, and replace the "No matching contact" line with the number of matches.
* The contact lookup tells the card apart two cases it currently reports the same way: "several contacts match" and "you are not allowed to see this contact".
* Inbound calls and their recordings attach to a contact when several share the number, using the rule below.
* Tests for one match, several matches, several matches with one recently contacted, and a rep who cannot see one or all of the matches.

Not included: preventing or merging duplicate contacts, which belongs to ENG-6551. The "create a lead from an unknown caller" prompt in ENG-12495 must keep showing only when nobody matched, not when several did.

## How it should work

* One match: unchanged.
* Several matches: the card lists up to two names, then "and N more". The contact with the most recent call or text on that number comes first.
* Attaching the call: if exactly one of the matching contacts had a call or text with the workspace on that number in the last 30 days, attach the inbound call and its recording to that contact. If none did, or more than one did at the same most recent time, leave the call unattached as today. Never pick arbitrarily. This narrows the "inbound matching never chooses arbitrarily" rule set in ENG-12257; it does not remove it.
* No matches, a withheld number, or a failed lookup: unchanged.
* The same attach rule applies everywhere an inbound call resolves a contact by phone number, so the card and the saved call agree.

## Who can do what

A rep only ever sees the names of contacts they are allowed to view. If a number matches several contacts and the rep can view only some, the card shows only those. If they can view none, the card behaves as it does today and reveals nothing, including the number of matches. Attaching the call to a contact happens on the server and does not depend on which rep answered.

## Done when

- [ ] A call from a number saved on two contacts shows both names on the card instead of "Unknown caller", with the recently contacted one first.
- [ ] The card never says "No matching contact" when there was at least one match the rep can see.
- [ ] That call and its recording appear on the timeline of the contact the team called or texted on that number in the last 30 days.
- [ ] With no recent contact on the number, the call stays unattached and the card still shows the names.
- [ ] A rep with own-only or team-only contact access never sees the name of a contact outside their access, and cannot tell that hidden matches exist.
- [ ] Single-match and no-match calls behave exactly as before.
- [ ] Browser QA covers the card for one, two and three or more matches.

## Implementation context

* The card's name comes from `useIncomingCaller` (`apps/web/components/crm/call/incoming/use-incoming-caller.ts`), which only accepts `status === 'single'`. The copy lives in `incoming-call-card.tsx` in the same folder.
* `findContactByPhone` in `apps/web/trpc/routers/crm/contact.ts` returns `ambiguous` both for more than one match and for every permission failure (no scope, empty team, owner outside scope). It needs a distinct status for several visible matches that carries the visible contacts.
* The server match is `lookupContactByPhone` / `findContactByPhone` in `apps/web/lib/crm/contact-phone-lookup.ts`, used by `inbound-voice-processor.ts` (call row link and voice message link), `app/api/voice/status/route.ts` and `app/api/webhooks/sendblue/call-log/route.ts`. It returns nothing for more than one match.
* Evidence from the reported case (workspace `<uuid>`): outbound call `<uuid>` at 15:26 UTC on 1 Oct was linked to contact `<uuid>` because it was dialled from the record. The inbound call back `<uuid>` at 15:33 UTC has no contact, and neither does its voice message `<uuid>`. The second contact on the same number is `<uuid>`. The rep has workspace-wide contact view, so permissions were not the cause.
* The recent-contact check can read the `call` table (`to_number` / `from_number` with a non-null `contact_id`) and the workspace's text messages for that number. Keep it to one indexed lookup; the inbound path must not slow down a ringing call.

relatedSnapshot.title: Let a released number be reassigned to the same rep
relatedSnapshot.description:
> **Context.** Glossary: master ticket ENG-12250. For THIS ticket: when a phone number is released we do not delete the record, we mark it deleted and keep the row. But the database rule that stops a rep having two numbers **counts the deleted row too**. So a rep who has ever had a number released can never be given another one. The error tells them to contact support. Why it matters: this will happen during rollout, when we are assigning numbers to a whole team and getting some of it wrong the first time.

**Size:** S · **Design:** none · **Blocked by:** ENG-12263 · **MVP**

### Overview

After this ticket, releasing a rep's number frees them to be assigned a new one, with no support ticket.

### Problem

`validateMemberPhoneNumberLimit` (`apps/web/trpc/routers/phone-numbers.ts:120-152`) deliberately does not exclude deleted rows, because it is matching the database rule exactly. The rule itself is what needs changing. There is already a cleanup script in the repository (`apps/web/scripts/cleanup-orphaned-phone-assignments.ts`) for unpicking this by hand, which tells you how often it happens.

### Solution

* Change the database rule so it only counts numbers that are not deleted.
* Update the matching check in the code, and delete the now-unnecessary error message.
* Run the existing cleanup script against any workspace already stuck.

### Scope

* In: the database rule, the code check, clearing existing stuck assignments.
* Out of scope: everything else about releasing numbers, including the Sendblue billing follow-up, which stays as it is.

### Acceptance criteria

1. A rep whose number was released can be assigned a new one immediately.
2. A rep still cannot hold two active numbers at once.
3. Workspaces currently stuck are cleared, and the number of rows fixed is reported.

relatedSnapshot.title: Always save a person's phone number: normalise it, never reject it
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

A person is always saved with the phone number they gave, from a workflow or the API. Acquisity normalises the number when it can and keeps it as typed when it can't. A phone number never stops a person from being created or updated.

## Problem

Since Acquisity/Acquisity#6663 (merged 30 Sep, ENG-14343), the workflow person step refuses the whole write with "phone must be a valid phone number" when the phone fails strict validation. ENG-14343 asked for phones to be normalised and matched "in any common format". It did not ask for numbers to be rejected; that was added during review in commit `82e4dbbc7a` ("validate phones before workflow writes").

What it cost in the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace between 30 Sep and 2 Oct:

* 40 workflow runs failed across three workflows (website and Fast-Track intake, webinar sign-up, lead tool result).
* 17 website sign-ups were not created at all, even though each had a valid email. Others were not updated.
* The workflows have been changed to check the phone first and leave it off when it is rejected, and the 40 runs were replayed. Nobody is missing now, but 19 people are saved without their phone.
* Of those 19 numbers, 16 are the right length for a US number but fail the strict check. 3 are too short (8 or 9 digits).

Forms get typos, test numbers and numbers typed without a country code. Losing the lead, or their number, over that is worse than storing an imperfect number.

## What's included

* `crm/upsert-contact`, `crm/update-contact` and the shared contact write helpers never fail because of the phone.
* A valid number is saved in E.164, as today.
* A number that is the right length but not strictly valid is still normalised and saved.
* A number that can't be normalised is saved as typed and marked unverified, so the app can show it and a rep can fix it.
* Matching keeps working: a number that can't be normalised matches only on its exact typed form.
* Calls and texts keep their own checks. An unverified number can't be dialled or texted until it is fixed, and the app says why.
* The same rule applies to the public API person routes that use the shared write path.
* The run's error message names the step that stopped it, not an earlier "not found" that was carried past. Today these runs show "Contact not found" when the real error is the phone.

## Done when

- [ ] A workflow run with a valid email and the phone `12345678` creates the person with that phone stored, and the run succeeds.
- [ ] A 10-digit US-shaped number that fails strict validation is stored in E.164 and the run succeeds.
- [ ] `+44 7700 900123` and `<phone>` are still stored and matched as today.
- [ ] Texting or calling an unverified number is refused with a clear message, and no other behaviour of the dial and send gates changes.
- [ ] A failed run shows the error from the step that stopped it.
- [ ] Workflows saved before this change behave the same for valid phones.

## Open questions

* How to mark an unverified number. Recommended default: a flag on the phone row, shown as a small "check this number" hint on the person, with no new settings.
* Whether Find person should return "not found" for a number that can't be normalised, where it returns an error today. Recommended default: "not found", so workflows can branch on it.

## Implementation context

* The rejection sits in `apps/web/plugins/workflows/crm/steps/upsert-contact.ts` (three places that return "phone must be a valid phone number") and in `setPrimaryContactPhone` in `apps/web/plugins/workflows/crm/steps/contact-write-utils.ts`, which throws. The normaliser is `packages/db/src/phone-number-normalization.ts` (`normalizeE164PhoneNumber` returns null for anything not valid).
* `matchCrmPersonIdentity` returns `invalid_identity` for such a phone, which `crm/find-person` turns into a step error.
* After this ships, the 19 phones can be filled by replaying the saved run inputs. They are kept in the workflow run history for workflows `bc1d2fbf`, `db110a33` and `df1b25d6`. The build session for the Close automations move will do the replay.
* High-risk path: phone identity and the dial and send gates share this normaliser.

relatedSnapshot.title: CRM v2: text and call a deal's person from the deal record
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

A rep on a deal in the new CRM (record drawer or full deal page) can text the deal's person from the deal itself, the same way they can already call them. Today Text is missing on deals, and "Text back" on a call row jumps away to the person's page.

## Problem

Deals are where reps work, but texting means leaving the deal, finding the person and opening their Calls & Texts tab. With several people on one deal, it is easy to text the wrong one.

## User experience

* **Text in the action row**, next to Call, whenever calling is on for the workspace.
  * One linked person with a phone number: Text opens the deal's composer on Text, addressed to that person.
  * Several: Text asks which person (name and number), then opens the composer for the one picked.
  * None: Text is disabled and says why (no linked person, or no one has a phone number), in the same words as the deal's Call button. An opted-out person gets the person page's opt-out message.
* **The composer always shows who the text goes to** (name and number), so a deal with several people is never ambiguous.
* **Consent and do-not-contact rules are exactly the person page's.** An opted-out person shows the same "Texts are paused" block and cannot be sent to; a workspace with no phone number cannot text.
* **Text back from a call row** opens the deal's composer for the person that call was with. A call with no number, a number that matches no linked person, a number two linked people share, or a number that is not that person's texting number is never guessed: the rep sees a short message instead.
* **Call** keeps today's behaviour: one reachable person is called straight away, several are asked which.

## What's included

* The deal drawer and the full deal page, both behind the CRM v2 flag and the phone calling feature.
* Reuses today's text composer (templates, send later, placeholders, consent checks).
* Not included: texting several people at once, and texting a number other than a person's main number.

## Done when

* Text shows on a deal next to Call and follows the one, several and none rules above.
* The composer names the person and number the text will go to.
* An opted-out person cannot be texted from a deal, with the same message as the person page.
* Text back on a deal's call row opens the deal composer for that call's person, or explains why it cannot.
* Sending a text from a deal is tracked in product analytics (wired and unit-tested; not yet seen landing in PostHog).
* Checked in the browser in light and dark, in the drawer and on the full page, without sending a real text.

## Implementation context

* Follow-up to Acquisity/Acquisity#6564 (ENG-14192). Splits out the "A deal's drawer texts the main contact directly" item from ENG-14191.
* ENG-14230 touches the same record composer; merge carefully.

relatedSnapshot.title: Find a person by any of their emails or phone numbers, however the number is typed
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

A rep who types an email address or a phone number into search lands on the right person, whichever of that person's addresses or numbers it is and however they typed the number. When the match is on a second email or phone, the list shows that value so the rep can see why the person came up. Conversations search gets the same reach.

## Problem

Asked on the 30 Sep migration call: "people sign up with different email addresses... are we able to search for leads via related emails and phone numbers?" Another rep searched People for existing leads, found nothing and created new people, which made duplicates.

Checked on 1 Oct against main and production (read-only). The picture is better than assumed on the call, with three real gaps:

* **Already works:** People search matches every email and phone stored on a person, not only the first. In AI Acquisition Sales Team that is 10,387 extra emails and 6,297 extra phone numbers.
* **Gap 1, phone format.** Phone search is a plain text match. 99% of the 138,583 numbers are stored as `<phone>`, so typing `07700 900912`, `(07700) 900-912` or `7700 900 912` finds nobody. This is the most likely reason a rep "cannot find" someone who is there.
* **Gap 2, no reason shown.** When a person matches on a second email or phone, the row shows only their first email and phone, so it looks like a wrong result.
* **Gap 3, Conversations.** Conversations search cannot find anyone by email, and matches a phone only when it is the number that conversation used, not the person's other numbers. The person picker when creating a deal cannot search by phone at all.

Two neighbouring causes are owned elsewhere: the New person form has no duplicate check (ENG-6551), and two records for the same human are only brought together by merging (ENG-14590 suggests them).

## User experience

* **People search:** typing `07700 900912`, `+44 7700 900912` or `7700900912` finds the same person. Any stored email or phone finds its person, as today.
* **Why it matched:** when the match is on a second email or phone, that value is shown in the Email or Phone column in place of the first one, with a small "Other" tag. Hovering the tag says "Another email on this person". Clearing the search restores the usual values.
* **Conversations search:** typing any email or phone that belongs to a person finds their conversation.
* **Creating a deal:** the person picker finds people by phone as well as by name and email.

**Design.** Interactive kit: People list. Anyone with the link can open it. It takes about 15 seconds to load. The attached screenshots show the same states.

What to try in it, typing into the search box at the top right of the People list:

* `07700 900912`, `(07700) 900-912` or `+44 7700 900912`: finds Name 5 by her second phone. The Phone column shows that number with an "Other" tag.
* `<email>`: finds Name 6 by his second email, shown in the Email column with an "Other" tag.
* `7946 0321`: finds Name 100 by his first phone, with no tag.
* Hover an "Other" tag for its tooltip. Clear the search to see the usual values return.
* The moon button bottom right switches light and dark.

## What's included

* Format-free phone matching in People search, and in Companies search where a company has phones.
* The "Other" tag in the People list.
* Email and any-phone matching in Conversations search.
* Phone matching in the deal form's person picker.
* Not included: a global search across the whole app (none exists today), a "related people" panel on the record, blocking duplicates on create, and bringing over extra Close contacts that were not imported.

## How it should work

* A search made only of digits, spaces, brackets, plus, dots and dashes, with at least three digits, is treated as a phone search and compared as digits. A leading 0 is ignored, so national and international forms both match.
* Search results stay within what the rep may see. The "Other" value comes from the person's own row, so nothing new is exposed.
* Search stays under a second in a workspace with more than 150,000 people. The digits match must be indexed, not scanned.

## Done when

- [ ] A person stored as `<phone>` is found by `07700 900912`, `(07700) 900-912`, `+44 7700 900912` and `7700900912`.
- [ ] A person found by their second email or phone shows that value with the "Other" tag, in the list and after sorting.
- [ ] Conversations search finds a person by an email, and by a phone number they have never been texted or called on.
- [ ] The deal form's person picker finds a person by phone.
- [ ] A rep limited to their own records never sees a person outside their access through search.
- [ ] People search for a phone number returns in under a second in AI Acquisition Sales Team, measured on the read replica.
- [ ] A search that matched on an "Other" email or phone is tracked through the repo's activation tracking skill, and the event is verified landing in PostHog.
- [ ] Browser QA in light and dark, compared with the attached design.

## Implementation context

* People, Companies and the Conversations "To" picker all go through `buildRecordSearchCondition` (`apps/web/lib/crm/record-search.ts`); emails and phones are matched in `communicationCondition` (`apps/web/lib/crm/record-search-relations.ts`) with `ILIKE` on `crm_email.email` and `crm_telephone.number`.
* feat(crm): search people, companies and deals through a trigram index (ENG-14533) (ENG-14533) moved record search onto a trigram index that already includes secondary emails and phones. The cheapest route is to add the digits form of each phone to that indexed text, not to build a second index.
* Conversations already has a digits-aware phone match, limited to the conversation's own number: `normalizeConversationSearch` (`apps/web/lib/crm/conversation-list-cursor.ts`) and `packages/db/src/repositories/conversation-list-context-query.ts`. Coordinate with ENG-14574, which is changing the same queries.
* Deal form picker: `getContactsForDeals` in `apps/web/trpc/routers/crm/contact.ts` has no phone match and no deleted-record filter.
* The inbound caller lookup (`apps/web/lib/crm/contact-phone-lookup.ts`) already compares digits and is the behaviour to copy.
* People rows already load every email and phone, so the "Other" tag needs no new query.
* Any new index on `crm_telephone` must be built without locking the table.
* **Building to the design.** Port the look and behaviour into the app's People list; never import kit files. Kit source: `kit/src/screens/crm-contacts.tsx` on design library branch `crm-call-fixes-2026-10-01` (commit e0fd97a), helpers `personHit`, `digitsOf` and `OtherTag`.
  * The "Other" tag: 11px tertiary text in a 5px-radius bordered chip on the frame grey, never a coloured pill (it is a label, not a status). It sits right of the value and never wraps; the value truncates first.
  * The matched value is shown in primary text in place of the first email or phone, in that same column. If the column is hidden the row still appears, with no tag.
  * Name 7 wording: "Another email on this person" and "Another phone on this person".
  * Only one "Other" value is shown per row: email wins if both match.
  * Kit-only, not for production: the two demo people with a second email or phone, and the suggestion menu under the search box (it already exists in the app).

relatedSnapshot.title: A voicemail and a text from the same number split into two separate conversations
relatedSnapshot.description:
> **Context.** Glossary: master ticket ENG-12173. For THIS ticket: when someone leaves a voicemail, we store it as a message in a conversation thread. When a rep later texts that same person from the same number, the code cannot find that existing thread, so it creates a second one. The rep ends up with the same person in two separate conversations. Why it matters: a closer looking at a contact sees a fragmented history, and the more they use the product the worse it gets.

**Size:** S/M · **Design:** none · **Blocked by:** nothing (ships right behind ENG-12251)

### How it was found

Elis found this while auditing PR #5900 on ENG-12251 and flagged it rather than fixing it inside an unrelated PR, which was the right call. He raised it because the underlying question looked like a product decision. **James has settled it: a voicemail and a text with the same person on the same number are one conversation, and this is a bug.**

### The defect

Deterministic, not a race. No concurrency needed.

* `InboundVoiceProcessor` (`apps/web/lib/services/inbound-voice-processor.ts:1114-1147`) creates the thread for a voicemail with `sourceType: 'sms'` and `sourceProvider: 'twilio'`, and **never sets** `twilioPhoneNumber`. Its own lookup omits the line too, so it is self-consistent and never noticed.
* The outbound recorder's thread lookup requires `eq(twilioPhoneNumber, ourLine)` (`outbound-message-recording.ts:534`). A voicemail-created thread has that column empty, so the predicate can never match it.
* Result: the first outbound text to a person who has left a voicemail always creates a second thread.

**This becomes reachable the moment** ENG-12251 **(PR #5900) merges**, because before that PR outbound never created threads at all. It is not a pre-existing production symptom, it is one that arrives with that merge, which is why it should land close behind it.

### Fix

Two options were on the table. **Take the first.**

1. **Make the voicemail path record the line it came in on.** Fixes the data at the source, keeps the outbound predicate strict, and means anything else reading threads by line also starts working. Preferred.
2. Loosen the outbound predicate to also match threads with an empty line. Rejected: it hides bad data rather than fixing it, and a thread with no line recorded is wrong regardless of who reads it.

Also needed:

* **Backfill existing voicemail-created threads.** Going forward-only leaves every historic voicemail thread still splitting. Derive the line from the voicemail's own message rows or the linked call record. Where it genuinely cannot be derived, leave it empty rather than guessing, and report the count.
* **Merge threads that have already split** where a voicemail thread and a text thread exist for the same contact and line. Report how many were merged. If merging turns out to be more than a small job, split that into its own follow-up and say so, but do not leave it undone silently.
* Throttle the backfill. The job queue absorbs roughly 10 to 12 executions per minute per workspace.

### Scope

* In: recording the line on voicemail-created threads, the backfill, merging already-split threads, tests covering voicemail-then-text on the same number.
* Out of scope: the Conversations tab itself (ENG-12277), and any change to how voicemails are stored beyond the missing line. Note that voicemails are filed with `sourceType: 'sms'`, which is odd but is not what this ticket is fixing.

### Acceptance criteria

1. A voicemail followed by an outbound text to the same person on the same number lands in **one** thread, not two.
2. That holds in both orders: voicemail first then text, and text first then voicemail.
3. Existing voicemail threads are backfilled with their line where it can be derived, and left empty rather than guessed where it cannot. The counts are reported.
4. Contacts already split across two threads are merged, with the count reported, or the remaining work is split into a named follow-up.
5. A voicemail on a line with no rep assigned still records the line.
6. A test covers the voicemail-then-text case so this cannot regress.

### Design (Name 8)

Data-merge ticket — for reference, how a unified thread should render once voicemail and text land in one conversation: 38 · conversations — call thread and 19 · conversations — default + call detail.

relatedSnapshot.title: Link every call to the Person and Deal
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Every new call keeps a durable link to the Person it was with and, when known, the Deal it was about.

## Problem

Contact matching works for many calls, but the durable call record does not own the Person or Deal relationship. Deal cannot safely be reconstructed from a phone number because one Person may have several Deals.

## Proposed fix

Persist the known Person and optional Deal when the call begins, then preserve them through provider callbacks, voice-message creation and activity rendering.

## What's included

* Outbound calls from Person, Deal, dialler or call control.
* Inbound calls using existing unambiguous matching or stub-contact behaviour.
* Optional Deal when initiating context supplies one.
* Name 12 and retry updates preserving links.
* Person and Deal history reading stored relationships.
* Workspace-scoped indexes and tests.

Not included: guessing between Deals, historical backfill, Smart Views, reporting, interaction dates or unknown-caller changes.

## Blocked by

* Make every call attempt leave a reliable record.

## How it should work

* Pass known Person or Deal into the call-creation boundary and validate workspace.
* Store relationships with the durable call attempt.
* Provider callbacks update call facts but never clear relationships.
* Inbound matching never chooses arbitrarily.
* If no Deal is known, leave it blank.
* Later phone edits do not move historical calls.
* Retries update the same call through provider identity.

## Who can do what

A rep can link only records they can access in the same workspace. Name 13 update only the call resolved through workspace and provider identity.

## What the user sees

A completed, failed or missed call appears once on the correct Person and on the Deal when one was explicitly known.

## Done when

- [ ] Person and optional Deal are stored on the durable call model.
- [ ] Power dialler and direct CRM paths preserve known IDs.
- [ ] Inbound calls retain safe contact behaviour.
- [ ] Provider updates cannot erase or cross-link.
- [ ] Histories display calls without phone rematching.
- [ ] Tests cover multiple Deals, unknown and edited numbers, retries and cross-workspace IDs.
- [ ] Browser QA proves Person and Deal call placement.

## Open questions

None: ambiguous Deal remains blank.

## Expected outcome

A call remains attached to the customer context in which it happened.

relatedSnapshot.title: A contact can end up with two primary phone numbers
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Nothing prevents a contact from having two numbers both marked as the primary one. When that happens, the CRM has to guess which is really primary, and different parts of the app can guess differently.

## Problem

Several routes can each mark a number as primary: merging contacts, a CSV import, and editing a contact directly. Two of them running close together can leave a contact with two primary numbers and no way to tell which is correct.

That matters in two visible places. Local time is worked out from the primary number, so the wrong pick shows the wrong time. The dialler calls the primary number, so the wrong pick calls the wrong phone.

Today the code copes by repairing the mess whenever it notices, keeping one and moving the others out of the way. That works but it is cleaning up after a problem the database should not allow in the first place.

## Proposed fix

Make the database enforce it, so a contact can only ever have one primary number.

## What's included

Tidying existing contacts that already have more than one, and adding the constraint.

## Blocked by

None: can start immediately.

## How it should work

Any attempt to create a second primary number for the same contact is rejected by the database, whichever route it came from, including two routes running at the same time.

## Who can do what

No permission change.

## What the user sees

Local time and the dialler consistently use the same number, and it is the one the contact record shows as primary.

## Done when

- [ ] Contacts that currently have more than one primary number are corrected to a single one.
- [ ] The database prevents a second primary number for the same contact.
- [ ] Deleted numbers are excluded, so removing a number frees the slot properly.
- [ ] The constraint is added without blocking writes while it is created.

## Open questions

Once the database enforces this, does the existing repair code stay as a safety net or become a simple check? Recommended default: keep it as a safety net and update its note, since it costs little and covers older data paths.

Separately, email addresses have exactly the same shape and the same gap. Worth deciding whether to fix both together or file the email one once this proves out.

## Expected outcome

One contact, one primary number, guaranteed rather than repaired.

## Implementation context

The constraint should be a partial unique index on the contact, limited to the primary slot and excluding deleted rows, and given an explicit name per the repo's migration conventions.

Two operational notes. Use the migration runner rather than pushing the schema directly, because this is a constraint change. And create the index without locking the table, since writes to it are frequent.

The existing repair logic lives in the phone-plan helper and has unit tests. Its note currently points at this ticket, so update it either way once the constraint exists.

> **Context.** Glossary: master ticket ENG-12173. For THIS ticket: reps currently have no always-available way to start a call; there are Call buttons on individual records, but nothing global. You are building the phone icon in the top right of the app (copy the Close screenshot linked below, that is exactly the look we want). The good news: the actual calling machinery already exists and works. `startCall` from `call-provider.tsx` places a call, and the call bar UI appears automatically. Your job is the button + panel + a dial pad that feeds a clean phone number into that existing function. "**E.164**" just means the international phone format (<phone>). "**Caller ID**" = the number the person being called sees. Why it matters: this is the front door of the whole phone system, and the first thing every rep touches.

**Size:** M · **Design:** needed (polished UI depends on the ENG-10004 design; a functional version may ship behind the feature flag first)
**How it should look (Close reference):** the phone popover (screenshot at top) and dialling a number not in the CRM: <url> and <url>

### Overview

Reps get a phone icon at the top right of the app, on every page. Clicking it opens a small panel (the phone popover) with a dial pad. They can type or paste any phone number and call it immediately, without leaving whatever page they are on. The panel stays available as they move around the app.

### Problem

There is no always-available place to start a call. There is no way at all to dial a number that is not saved in the CRM. Reps coming from Close expect a phone button that is always one click away.

### Solution

Build a global phone popover, mounted once at the app level so it exists on every page and survives navigation. It contains a dial pad with paste support. Numbers are cleaned up into the international format (E.164: the standard format with a country code, like <phone>); when no country code is given, the account's country is used. Pressing call starts a call through the existing call flow, and the existing call bar appears. Dialling is disabled while a call is already active.

Calling numbers that are not in the CRM is allowed. After such a call ends, the rep is prompted to quickly create a contact for that number; declining leaves the call logged without a contact.

Security is enforced on the server, not just in the UI: the procedures that place a call verify the user's phone-calling feature access, their permission to make calls, and that the outgoing number belongs to them. Hiding the button is never the only protection.

Usage tracking ships from day one: instrument activation tracking using the repo's `instrument-activation-tracking` skill, at minimum the L1 "tool.opened" event. Tracking only counts as done once the events are verified as landing in PostHog.

Technical notes:

* Mount next to `<CallBar/>` in `apps/web/app/(saas)/providers.tsx` (route-persistent, same pattern as the call bar).
* E.164 normalization with organization-country fallback; calls go through `startCall`.
* Server-side enforcement: `FEATURES.PHONE_CALLING` + `voice.make_call` + caller-ID ownership checked in the call path.
* Design comes from ENG-10004 (Name 8 CRM page 1444-65385).

### Scope

* In: the global phone button and popover shell, dial pad with paste and number normalization, call start wiring, disabled state during an active call, unknown-number quick-create-contact prompt, server-side permission checks on the call path, activation tracking.
* Out of scope: caller-ID switcher and recording toggle (separate popover ticket), audio settings and first-use setup flow (separate ticket), any power dialler behavior.

### Acceptance criteria

1. When a user with calling access is anywhere in the app, then the phone icon is visible top right, and clicking it opens the popover.
2. When a number is typed or pasted in a common local format without a country code, then it is normalized using the account's country, and the E.164 result is shown before dialling.
3. When the rep presses call, then the call starts through the existing call flow and the call bar appears.
4. When a call is already active, then the dial controls are disabled with a clear indication of why.
5. When the rep calls a number that is not in the CRM, then the call completes normally, and after hangup a prompt offers to create a contact; declining leaves the call logged without a contact.
6. When a user lacks the calling feature or the make-call permission, then the phone button is hidden AND a direct server request to place a call is rejected server-side.
7. When a call request carries an outgoing number the user does not own, then the server rejects it.
8. When the rep navigates between pages with the popover open or a call running, then the popover and call survive the navigation.
9. The "tool.opened" event fires when the popover opens and is verified as landing in PostHog.

### Design (Name 8)

* 23 · phone ready — the phone popover as it opens from the top-bar phone button: caller ID, auto-record toggle, paste-to-call field + dial button
* 26 · phone keypad — the keypad view

This shipped before the revised design landed — treat 23/26 as the parity target when touching the popover. Full screen map on master ENG-12173.

relatedSnapshot.title: Extend the Me filter to contacts and companies, and add linked-record fields to deal views
relatedSnapshot.description:
> **Context.** Glossary: master ticket ENG-12174. For THIS ticket: a "Me" filter means a shared view can say owner = whoever is looking, so ONE shared "my leads" view shows each rep their own records instead of the team maintaining a copy per rep. Every shared closing view in our Close workspace uses this. Good news: the token (`__current_user__`) already exists and works for deals and tasks; contacts and companies just never pass the current user into their query builders, so half this ticket is threading one value through. The other half: deal views can currently only say whether a linked contact EXISTS, not show anything about them; you are adding linked-contact fields (has a phone, title) and company fields as columns and filters on deal views. Why it matters: it is the second of the two views tickets on the SDR migration critical path (one shared dial view for the whole team).

**Size:** M · **Design:** pattern-reuse · **Blocked by:** nothing
**How it should work (Close reference):** the Me filter on shared views: <url> (User filters and the Me filter section)
**Audit evidence:** ENG-12178 findings, "Me" and "Cross-entity" rows. Real-usage proof: every shared closing view in our Close workspace filters "Closer: Me"; one shared view serves the whole team.

### Overview

One shared view saved with owner set to "Me" shows each rep their own records: rep A sees A's, rep B sees B's, from the same view. Deal views also gain fields from the deal's linked contact and company, so an SDR pipeline view can show and filter on "contact has a phone", contact title, or company attributes.

### Problem

The `__current_user__` token already exists and resolves at query time for DEALS and TASKS (list, kanban, counts, export). Contacts and companies never thread `currentUserId` into their query builders, and their owner pickers only offer concrete users. On the cross-entity side, deal views expose only has-linked booleans, no linked-record attributes.

### Solution

* Thread `currentUserId` through the contact and company query builders and list/count/export procedures; add "Current user (Me)" to their owner picker (same pattern the deal picker uses).
* Add linked-record fields to deal views as columns and filters: linked contact has a phone (yes/no), contact title, contact email present, and company name/industry/size fields, joined through the deal's links in the existing view query builders.
* Row permissions unchanged: a Me view shows each rep only rows they may see anyway.

### Scope

* In: Me token on contacts + companies end to end, picker options, linked-contact and company fields on deal views (columns + filters), tests per surface.
* Out of scope: "my team"/role tokens, cross-entity fields on non-deal views, the AI prompts' Me emission (ENG-12229 owns that), editing linked data from the deal row.

### Acceptance criteria

1. A single shared contact view with owner = Me shows rep A only A's contacts and rep B only B's, from the same view; same for companies.
2. Me works in list, counts, and export for contacts and companies (parity with the existing deal behavior).
3. A deal view can filter "linked contact has a phone number" and show contact title and company fields as columns with correct values.
4. Sorting and filtering on the new cross-entity fields is correct on a fixture org.
5. No rep sees any row through a Me view they could not see elsewhere.

### Design (Name 8)

* 32 · smart view edit filters — the Me token appears as a normal filter value in this editor
* 40 · people list view · 41 · companies list view — the list surfaces where linked-record fields become columns

Full screen map on master ENG-12174.

relatedSnapshot.title: Add texts, emails, meetings and tasks to the rep activity numbers
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Delivery scope correction · 10 September 2026

The replacement Acquisity/Acquisity#6347 and Acquisity/Acquisity#6348 do not implement call/text/email/meeting/task activity attribution or the SDR activity cards. The previous reconciliation paragraph incorrectly assigned this work to those replacements and is superseded by this correction. This issue remains separately owned and outstanding; merging those PRs does not satisfy its acceptance criteria.

Pipeline-scoped call reporting also remains outstanding after the reporting-groups replacement; it must be explicitly covered in the SDR reporting delivery plan. Preserve the source-record, human-versus-automation and deduplication requirements below.

This correction changes delivery attribution only. Existing ownership, priority, status, dependencies and remaining acceptance criteria are unchanged.

> **Context.** Glossary: master ticket ENG-12250. For THIS ticket: the earlier tickets give us calling numbers. Close's version of this screen covers five families: leads, calls, emails, text messages and opportunities. This ticket adds the rest, once the underlying records are trustworthy, which is why it is blocked by most of the data tickets. Why it matters: a rep who makes few calls but sends many texts is working, and a calls-only screen makes them look idle.

**Size:** M · **Design:** pattern-reuse · **Blocked by:** ENG-11568, ENG-12251, ENG-12252, ENG-12253, ENG-11563 · **Nice to have**
**How it should work (Close reference):** <url> see the metric categories

### Overview

After this ticket, the rep numbers cover texts, emails, meetings and completed tasks alongside calls.

### Problem

Only calls are counted. The other channels either had no reliable record (the data tickets fix that) or have a counting trap.

**The counting trap, and this ticket must handle it explicitly.** Several kinds of activity deliberately write **more than one timeline row for a single real action**, so the activity shows up on the contact and on the deal and on any linked records. Meetings write to the deal, the contact, and every linked contact and deal (`apps/web/trpc/routers/appointments.ts:2974-3072`). Tasks write to as many as three records. Payments write three. There is no shared id on those rows tying them back to the one thing that happened, so **a naive count overcounts meetings, tasks and payments by a factor of two to four.** Calls and texts do not have this problem.

### Solution

* Add counts for texts sent, emails sent, meetings held and tasks completed, using the trustworthy records from the data tickets.
* **Count real actions, not rows.** Either group by the underlying record id held in the row's metadata, or add a shared id at write time so one action is one row to count. **Prefer the second:** it is a small change and it makes every future count correct by default.
* Exclude automated activity by default, using the shared helper from ENG-12252, with a toggle to include it. An automated text is not rep activity.
* Keep each channel a separate column rather than a combined "activities" number, matching Close.

### Scope

* In: the four extra channels, the double-counting fix, the automation exclusion and toggle.
* Out of scope: email opens and clicks, which are not tracked for CRM-sent email; cold email campaign metrics, which are a separate product area with their own reporting.

### Acceptance criteria

1. Rep numbers include texts sent, emails sent, meetings held and tasks completed.
2. A meeting linked to a deal and two contacts counts **once**, not three times. Verified against a deliberately constructed case.
3. Automated activity is excluded by default and can be included with a toggle.
4. Every channel's count matches a hand-written query for one rep over one day.
5. Text messages sent as iMessage and as normal text messages are both counted, and can be told apart.

relatedSnapshot.title: Add communication count and presence filters to contact and deal views
relatedSnapshot.description:
Split 4/4 of ENG-12233. Independent — uses existing count and date operators, base `main`, no dependency on the other splits.

### Problem

Views cannot answer two everyday questions. First, volume and reachability: how many emails or SMS a person has exchanged, whether they have been communicated with at all, and whether we even hold an email address or phone number for them. Second, deal views have none of the email or meeting recency that contact views already have — `lastEmailActivityAt`, `lastMeetingAt` and `hasMeetingScheduled` are contact-only (`config.type === 'contact'` in `advanced-query-builder.ts`). **That second problem is no longer solved by this ticket; it is** ENG-12641**.**

### Solution

New built-in filterable fields, following the ENG-12179 pattern (field key → query builder → field config → index):

**Counts and presence** (contact and deal):

* Email count, SMS count — numeric operators, reusing `buildCountMetricCondition`.
* Total communications across any channel — some / none.
* Has at least one email address; has at least one phone number.

**Deal extension:** moved to ENG-12641 — `lastEmailActivityAt`, `lastMeetingAt` and `hasMeetingScheduled` remain contact-only after this ticket.

**Deal grain for the count/presence fields:** one answer per deal over the UNION of its linked contacts (count summed, presence true when any linked contact has the detail) — deliberately not the `canonicalDealContactId` pick that `call-history-fields.ts` uses, since these fields have no column that a picked record must agree with. Reconciling that difference with `Call count` is ENG-12642.

Presence checks read the contact's own `emails` / `telephones`; counts read communication history. Both grains must be stated explicitly in the field help text so "has an email" on a deal is unambiguous.

### Scope

* In: the count and presence fields above on contact and deal views, filterable and savable, sample-mode evaluators so the filters are honest before a workspace has real data, and DB-backed tests that match hand counts at each grain.
* Out: the deal-side extension of the three existing recency fields (ENG-12641).
* Out: smart-field COLUMNS (ENG-12235), filter group UI (ENG-12231), the other ENG-12233 splits' fields.

### Acceptance criteria

1. Email count, SMS count, communications some/none, has-email and has-phone all match hand counts on the fixture org (parent AC4).
2. Counts are correct at the stated grain: a contact's own communications vs a deal's linked-contact communications, with no double counting when several linked contacts share a thread.
3. **DESCOPED** — deal-view support for `lastEmailActivityAt`, `lastMeetingAt` and `hasMeetingScheduled` moved to ENG-12641**.** Those three predicates hardcode `crmContactTable.id` in `advanced-query-builder.ts`, so extending them is a refactor of existing contact-only code rather than new field work. Split out at review on PR #5984 to keep this ticket to one shape of change; the parent's "email/meeting recency extended to deal views" is delivered by ENG-12641, not here.
4. Soft-deleted contacts, communications and links are excluded everywhere.
5. Every new field is savable into shared views and appears in the Add-filter picker with readable labels (parent AC6).
6. Large-org lists filtered on these fields stay responsive, verified by query plan showing indexed reads (parent AC7).

Parent: ENG-12233.
